key_insight: The paper turns hyperfine intermediate states from a source of error into a resource to speed up adiabatic CNOT gates while preserving high fidelity.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical route to faster, robust quantum logic in Rydberg-atom hardware under realistic decoherence constraints.
method: Use an EIT-based adiabatic CNOT protocol with hyperfine intermediate states (HISs).
Exploit HISs to improve adiabaticity in the STAY pathway and accelerate transfer in the TRANSFER pathway.
Optimize pulse shapes and extend the model to include multiple decaying HISs and arbitrary state counts.
evidence_signal: In realistic cesium atomic setups, the optimized protocol achieves adiabatic gate fidelities above 0.9991 in 0.3903 μs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful pulse optimization and sensitivity to decay from multiple intermediate states in real hardware.
paper_title: Fast Adiabatic Quantum Gates via Hyperfine Intermediate States
